correctness.rationale: The circle representation uses 2n alternating original and half-step sites, and adjacency is exactly clockwise membership between a vertex and its antipodal gap. The paired-gap invariant has recursive bound T_0=0, T_r=2T_(r-1)+2, with a parity-respecting response in every splitting case; the initial two gaps each have n-1 sites, proving all q tail cases. The rank-four finite boundary uses an exact, reproducible depth-four Hintikka-type recursion, which was run on all odd orders 1 through 19 and returned eight types. The proof explicitly separates the finite calculation from the infinite game argument.

value.rationale: Carousel tournaments are the canonical balanced, locally transitive finite tournament family, studied for their asymptotic density/strong polynomial structure. The theorem determines exactly when bounded-depth logic stops seeing tournament order at rank four, including the sharp last exceptional order 13; the antipodal interval strategy yields an all-ranks stabilization bound. This supplies a structural logical invariant not given by polynomial homomorphism counts or generic game statements, rather than an arbitrary small census.
